89a2405f00029db1: KOTA TINGGI: Firefighters battling a peatland blaze along the Sebana Cove-Punggai bypass in Pengerang are expected to need another two days to completely extinguish the fire, which has burned 17 hectares.
Johor Fire and Rescue Department director Siti Rohani Nadir said firefighters had so far put out flames over 10 hectares of the affected area.
She said the department received a distress call at 5pm yesterday, prompting the deployment of 18 personnel from the Sebana Cove and Punggai fire stations.
"The fire has spread to the other side of the road, bringing the total area affected to 17 hectares.

"If the weather remains relatively calm and there are no strong winds, we expect the situation to be brought under control and the firefighting operation to be completed within another two days," she said after inspecting the operation today.
Siti Rohani said human activity could not be ruled out as a possible cause, particularly amid the current hot and dry weather.
She urged the public to refrain from open burning, saying even a small fire could quickly spread under such conditions.
Firefighters are using an excavator to dig trenches to contain the blaze, while water is being sprayed directly onto the affected areas.
Meanwhile, Tanjung Surat assemblyman Aznan Tamin, who spent about an hour inspecting the operation, also urged residents to stop open burning during the hot and dry spell.
"The fire started small but spread rapidly due to strong winds and the extreme heat.
"I strongly urge those in the area not to conduct open burning. Let us stop for the next month or two to prevent more fires," he said.
Aznan also urged parents to monitor their children and limit outdoor activities, while schools should temporarily suspend outdoor activities to safeguard pupils' health and safety.
99605d093a1dc218: SINGAPORE: Top ministers in Singapore will discuss ministerial salaries in parliament on Tuesday, a sensitive and closely watched topic in the city-state, where political office comes with high rates of pay in order to attract talent and deter graft.

Singapore pays its political leaders the highest salary in the world, with a junior minister taking home S$1.1 million (US$868,056) annually and the prime minister earning S$2.2 million (US$1.74 million) a year.
The salaries have not been adjusted since 2012, when ministers took a 36 per cent pay cut to allay public discontent about how much they earned.
High ministerial salaries are a sensitive issue among the population, where the median monthly income was just S$5,775 in 2025.
Meanwhile, inflation crept up to two per cent in July, with the central bank expecting the figure to remain elevated until the second half of 2027.
According to data from non-profit PoliticalSalaries.com, the Hong Kong chief executive is the second-highest earner globally with US$719,000 annually, followed by the Swiss president at US$606,000.
In comparison, the British prime minister makes US$230,000 while President Donald Trump earns US$400,000.
After the 2012 pay cut, the government reviewed salaries again in 2017 but chose not to adopt a committee recommendation to hike.
A second review due in 2023 was deferred till now because of economic uncertainty.
On Tuesday, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Coordinating Minister for Public Services Chan Chun Sing will provide the government's response to a committee's recommendations on ministerial salaries.
Lawmakers will debate the issue later in the week.

Singapore uses the salary of the top 1,000 Singaporean earners as a benchmark for ministerial pay, saying the qualities and abilities of the top 1,000 "reflect the desired calibre of the people whom Singapore needs for good government", according to the website of the country's Public Service Division.
The high salaries are meant to attract top talent and prevent corruption, and cases of graft by senior officials have been rare.
In a recent case, former transport minister S. Iswaran was jailed in 2024 for obstructing justice and receiving more than US$300,000 worth of gifts.
0dcd2c7aff4d02e2: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 7 — The public, particularly prospective homebuyers, are encouraged to check information on developers and housing projects through the TEDUH portal and mobile application before making a purchase decision to reduce the risk of encountering problems later.

The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) said TEDUH, developed by the National Housing Department (JPN), is a one-stop platform providing access to information such as developers’ licence status, advertising permit and developer’s licence (APDL), project progress and information related to private housing projects.

“Through the #TEDUHBersama campaign, the ministry aims to cultivate the practice of ‘check before you buy’ among the public, particularly prospective homebuyers, as an initial step to reduce the risk of dealing with unlicensed developers or making purchase decisions without knowing the actual status of a project,” the ministry said in a statement.

It added that the portal also provides facilities to check the status of private housing projects, including projects categorised as delayed, troubled or abandoned, as well as approved selling prices.

Users can also check certain approvals issued by the government, including extensions of time (EOT), verify the authenticity of related documents and submit housing development complaints to JPN for review and further action.

JPN director-general Dr Tan Awang Besar, in the same statement, said the public was advised to conduct checks before purchasing a house as it was one of the biggest financial commitments in a person’s life.
“This simple step is important to help buyers obtain accurate information, make decisions with greater confidence and reduce the risk of encountering problems later,” he said.
TEDUH was launched on Aug 11, 2017, and has since been progressively enhanced as a more comprehensive, transparent and user-friendly housing reference platform.
According to KPKT, the TEDUH portal recorded more than 45 million visitors in total as of August.
The public can access the TEDUH Portal via teduh.kpkt.gov.my or use the TEDUH mobile application. — Bernama
493957d296881538: LONDON, Sept 7 — British luxury carmaker Jaguar Land Rover announced Monday a voluntary redundancy scheme following months of turmoil caused by a cyberattack and US President Donald Trump’s sector-wide tariffs.
British media reported that up to 4,000 roles could be removed, equivalent to around 10 per cent of JLR’s global workforce of more than 40,000 people, according to its website.
The vast majority, around 34,000 staff, are based in the UK.

“As we deliver the next phase of our strategy we need to adapt to evolving global market conditions while targeting approximately £1.7 billion (RM9.3 billion) of savings over the next two years,” JLR said in a statement.

“We have informed our colleagues and trade union partners that JLR is opening a voluntary redundancy programme offering salaried and management team members the opportunity to leave the business,” it said.
JLR said it would provide further detail later Monday, and UK business minister Jonathan Reynolds is scheduled to meet with the company’s management early this week.
The restructuring comes one year after a major cyberattack halted JLR’s production in Britain and severely affected its finances.
Owned by India’s Tata Motors, JLR was forced to halt production for more than a month, costing the company £196 million.
Hit also by US tariffs, the carmaker posted a loss of £244 million for its fiscal year ending in March, compared with a net profit of £1.8 billion in 2024-25.
“We must further simplify our organisation, improve efficiency, and build greater resilience,” JLR said in its statement.
Seeking to move on from the cyberattack, the company last week opened orders for its new fully electric Range Rover.
It comes as European carmakers are facing increased pressure for their vehicles from Chinese manufacturers as the industry shifts toward electric vehicles.

German car giant Volkswagen said Thursday that its management and unions had agreed to axe a total of 100,000 jobs by the end of the decade, the biggest-ever restructuring in the global auto industry.
The company said it had approved a plan involving the reduction of around 50,000 jobs, on top of another 50,000 already agreed. — AFP
c3ae4415d7c5e384: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) continues to strengthen the nation’s higher education empowerment agenda by offering Loan Advance Payments (WPP) totaling RM1,500 to eligible new students to help cover part of the initial preparation costs for admission to public universities and polytechnics.
In a statement, PTPTN said the RM39.7 million scheme benefits 26,457 students entering bachelor’s degree programmes at public universities and polytechnics for the September 2026 intake.
“The WPP is available to Malaysian citizens who opted into the scheme when applying to public higher education institutions via UPUOnline or university websites.
“In addition, applicants’ parents or guardians must be recipients of Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and meet the specified eligibility criteria,” according to the statement.
From WPP’s introduction in 1999 until July 31, more than 1 million students have benefited from the initiative, with an allocation totaling RM1.48 billion, it said.

The agency, which operates under the Higher Education Ministry (MOHE), said applicants can check their offers via the myPTPTN mobile app and collect the cash at Bank Islam branches nationwide starting Sept 4 by presenting their WPP offer letter and MyKad.
“The WPP is valid for two months, from Sept 4 to Nov 3 (Tuesday),” it said, noting that third-party collection is not permitted.

Recently, PTPTN also reached out to students receiving the WPP offer through home visits in Tasek Gelugor, Penang, followed by the WPP handover ceremony for the Bukit Gelugor area, officiated by PTPTN Chairman Datuk Seri Norliza Abdul Rahim.

According to the statement, Norliza said in her speech that PTPTN remains committed to strengthening the higher education agenda by ensuring that access to education financing continues to be empowered and can be enjoyed by all layers of society regardless of background and socio-economic status.

“In line with that aspiration, PTPTN’s WPP is among the strategic initiatives implemented to provide early financial support to students, thereby helping to ease the financial burden on families in making preparations and meeting basic needs before students begin studies at public universities and polytechnics,” she said.

PTPTN also said that students who wish to apply for loans can submit applications online via the myPTPTN application during the application period set by each public university and polytechnic, to ensure applications are processed and approved accordingly.

PTPTN said students must have a National Education Savings Scheme (Simpan SSPN) account, which can be opened through the myPTPTN application, urging them to refer to the Student Affairs Division of their respective universities and polytechnics or contact PTPTN if they have any questions.
It said additional details on loan advances and educational financing can be obtained from the myPTPTN digital application for easier, faster, and safer services. — Bernama
7d7a8e20a356d703: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Passenger fares for the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) have not been finalised and an official announcement will be made by the end of this year, said Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL).

MRL said in a statement on the ECRL Facebook page today that a recently recirculated information on social media regarding the passenger fares is inaccurate and has never been verified by any authority.
The company said the official passenger fares for the ECRL will only be announced by the Ministry of Transport Malaysia once the relevant evaluation and approval processes are finalised.

MRL advised the public against making any assumptions or conclusions based on unverified information, and to instead refer to announcements made through official channels of the Ministry of Transport, MRL, and ECRL.
"The ECRL fares will be determined after taking into account the public interest, user affordability, as well as the value and quality of services to be offered,” it said.

MRL said that once operational, travel time between Kota Bharu and Gombak is expected to take around four hours, Kuala Terengganu to Gombak about three hours, and Kuantan to Gombak approximately one hour and 35 minutes.
"The ECRL not only offers a new transport option for the public, but will also transform mobility between the East Coast and the Klang Valley,” it said.
The first phase of the ECRL from Kota Bharu to Gombak is expected to begin operations this December. — Bernama
828c3c1149eb8533: TOKYO, Sept 7 — Tokyo tourist hotspot Shinjuku will impose a ban on more than half of its holiday rentals including homes on Airbnb after a surge in complaints about visitors, an official said Monday.
Known for its buzzing commercial and entertainment district, Shinjuku has around 4,000 short-term rentals, according to the ward’s official website. That is nearly 10 per cent of Japan’s total.
But its large residential population has become increasingly exasperated with tourists who fail to properly dispose of rubbish, smoke where they are not supposed to and make too much noise.
A Shinjuku official supervising holiday rentals told AFP that the district was “planning to revise the current ordinance... to ban private lodging” in residential zones and areas near schools.
“As the number of private lodging businesses has risen, complaints and troubles around them have increased,” the official said on customary condition of anonymity.
More than 50 per cent of short-term rentals in Shinjuku face a ban under the new rules, he said, adding that the plan would formally be announced by the Shinjuku mayor on Tuesday.
The policy will only apply to existing rentals, the official said. It is likely to result in the closure of around 2,000 properties, including an unknown number on Airbnb.
Japan aims to attract 60 million foreign tourists by 2030, up from 42 million in 2025, but overtourism has emerged as a major challenge.
Residents of Japan’s former imperial capital Kyoto and other hotspots have expressed annoyance at selfie-taking crowds as well as traffic congestion and soaring land prices.
In Shinjuku, the number of complaints over vacation rentals increased by around 40 per cent in the fiscal year to March, the official said.
“Many complaints are about the violation of trash disposal rules while others include smoking and trespassing,” he said.
American tourist Luke Jemison, 24, told AFP that the rules “make sense, because of noise”.
Masaru Sato, a Shinjuku resident in his 70s, said “many foreigners, including operators of private lodgings, don’t follow local rules”.
“This area gets dirty because the way they dispose of trash is very messy,” he told AFP.
AFP has contacted Airbnb for comment. Several hosts in Shinjuku declined interviews when contacted by AFP.

In July, the Japan Tourism Agency gave municipalities the right to regulate short-term lodgings if “a tranquil living and educational environment” is under threat or if they “hinder the maintenance of a permanent population and local community”.
Kyoto is also considering a ban on short-term lodging, but only for new rentals within residential and industrial areas.
Other global cities have cracked down on private lodgings available through online rental platforms.

That is partly due to overtourism concerns, but also because some residents say home-sharing websites for tourists deprive locals of apartments for long-term rent and push up prices for homes remaining on the market.
Barcelona, one of Europe’s most-visited cities, aims to ban apartment rentals to tourists by 2029 to ease a housing shortage.
Under rules introduced in 2023, New York prohibits rental periods of less than 30 days unless the host lives in the property. — AFP
18b7c3dc6c8dfebb: SHAH ALAM: The investigation into the roller coaster accident at Sunway Lagoon in Subang Jaya is expected to take at least three to four months to complete, said Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar.
He said the investigation was still ongoing, with the timeframe being the minimum period required to complete the probe.

"We are still examining the scene and expect the minimum timeframe to complete the investigation to be between three and four months," he said at a press conference at the Selangor Police Headquarters today.
He said the inquiry involved the Occupational Safety and Health Department, Fire and Rescue Department, forensic teams and several other agencies.
Police have recorded statements from theme park staff, roller coaster operators, injured and uninjured visitors, as well as medical personnel.
Shazeli said further interviews were expected to assist the investigation, particularly in determining the technical aspects of the incident.
On Aug 22, 10 visitors were injured in the roller coaster accident.
On Aug 27, Shazeli said police were investigating possible elements of negligence and sabotage in connection with the incident.
At about 9pm on the day of the incident, 22 visitors aged between 11 and 44, including foreign tourists, were on the ride.
Subang Jaya police chief Assistant Commissioner Wan Azlan Wan Mamat said all 10 victims suffered minor injuries and were taken to medical centres in the Subang Jaya area for treatment.
1deb707acb7ec450: KUALA LUMPUR: Yayasan Usahawan Malaysia (YUM) has urged stronger SME support, faster public-sector delivery and anti-corruption reforms in 2027 Budget amid global economic uncertainty.
For SMEs, the foundation said government assistance should reward measurable growth outcomes rather than programme participation.

YUM also called for the establishment of National SME Transformation Fund which is a multi-year facility to support businesses that invest in digital transformation and adoption of renewable energy efforts to promote long-term growth.
The foundation also proposes a National Business Approval Service Charter, with measurable turnaround times for agencies dealing directly with businesses.

On the government's reform agenda, the foundation proposed a permanent multi-agency task force chaired at a sufficiently senior level to identify and eliminate regulations that unnecessarily delay investment and business activity.
It also proposed that government ministries, agencies and government-linked companies adopt a 30-day payment standard for approved SME invoices wherever practicable.
At the regional level, the foundation said Malaysia should aggressively capture opportunities in semiconductors, cloud computing, data centres and cybersecurity, among others.

"The 2027 Budget should not merely ask how much the government can spend. It should ask how every ringgit spent can unlock another ringgit of private investment, create another Malaysian entrepreneur, raise productivity and strengthen confidence in our country," YUM chairman Datuk Nitesh Malani said in a statement.
"Malaysia does not lack talent, ideas or opportunities. What entrepreneurs need is speed, certainty, access and a government ecosystem that enables rather than obstructs growth," he added.
4b4fe06a9509307f: KUALA LUMPUR: The national junior women's hockey team fell to their third defeat after losing 1-0 to South Korea in the Elite Group of the Junior Asia Cup (JAC) in Inner Mongolia, China on Monday.
The only goal of the match was scored by Park So Yeon in the 45th minute.
Nasihin Nubli's team put up a better performance against the Koreans after suffering heavy defeats.
Malaysia were routed 6-1 by China and then thrashed 11-1 by India.
After three matches, Malaysia scored two goals and conceded 18.
Malaysia, who are bottom of the group, will wrap up the fixtures against Japan on Wednesday.
be24fdc48f14a9c4: GENEVA, Sept 7 — The United Nations rights chief warned Monday that artificial intelligence could pose an “existential threat to humanity”, demanding immediate action to reduce the risks.
Speaking before the UN Human Rights Council, Volker Turk warned that humans currently faced “unfamiliar, even unprecedented” threats to their rights.
“The need for AI governance is widely acknowledged, but where is the action?” he asked, warning that “delay only benefits the massive tech companies, their owners and enablers”.
Turk decried that “a handful of men has almost unlimited power over AI, which we are repeatedly told has unimaginable computing capacity”.
“They talk about freedom, but on closer inspection, this turns out to be little more than the freedom to exploit our data,” the rights chief said.
Turk warned in particular that “AI that escapes its testing environment or blackmails developers to prevent itself from being turned off, is AI that is too powerful”.

He appeared to be alluding to revelations in July that OpenAI agents had escaped supposedly controlled environments and had broken into servers of Hugging Face, a widely used platform where programmers share AI software.
That episode shook the tech world and revived calls for tighter regulation and oversight of AI.
Anthropic, Meta and other companies have reported similar incidents while testing agents.
“I share the concerns of industry insiders that advanced AI could pose an existential risk to humanity,” Turk said.
“I am calling here, today, for an all-out effort to put cast iron guarantees in place around the safety and security of AI, before it is too late.”
The UN rights chief said he would be writing to AI companies in coming days “to urge them to take the steps that are within their control to reduce risks now”.
At a minimum, he said, “we need countries hosting AI and those involved in its supply chains to come together around agreed red lines”.
“We need independent verification, and much stronger collaboration on security within the industry,” he said.
“We also need to consider the human rights impacts of AI on employment practices, on fundamental principles of democracy, and on our environment.” — AFP
3e77376e9e12c745: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — China accounted for nearly one-third of the RM10.3 billion in strategic collaborations and potential investments secured at the Malaysian Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition (MAHA) 2026.

Agriculture and Food Security Ministry’s Business Development and Investment Division Undersecretary Khalid Ibrahim said 17 memoranda of understanding (MoUs) worth RM3.2 billion were signed between Malaysian and Chinese parties.
The MoUs covered premium tropical fruits such as durian, jackfruit, pineapple, mangosteen and young fresh coconut.

“They also covered premium-grade seafood and fisheries products, advanced smart agriculture technologies, high-quality fertilisers and pesticides, as well as premium edible bird’s nest in raw, unclean and clean processed forms and speciality coffee products.

“All these products represent Malaysia’s premier agro-food exports to the Chinese market, supported by integrated cold-chain logistics to ensure optimal freshness and quality upon arrival,” he told Bernama Monday.

Meanwhile, First Secretary at the Agriculture Counsellor Office at the Malaysian Embassy in Beijing, China, Siti Zurianah Ismail said a total of 80 delegates from China attended MAHA 2026, marking the country’s second and largest participation since 2024.
“They comprised businessmen, wholesale associations, potential partners and investors,” she told Bernama on Monday before returning to Beijing.
Siti Zurianah said China also hosted two pavilions at MAHA 2026, showcasing more than 100 products.
Among the Chinese products that attracted visitors were honey, Halal beef jerky, yak bone marrow, drone technology and health supplements.
She said the strong Chinese participation reflected the growing interest in Malaysia’s agro-food sector, particularly in trade, investment, technology and market opportunities.

MAHA 2026, themed “Creating Value for Food Security”, was held at the Malaysia Agro Exposition Park Serdang (MAEPS) from Aug 28 to Sept 6 and recorded about 4.3 million visitors, including 1.7 million youths, as of Sept 5.

At the closing ceremony, Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said MAHA 2026 had secured strategic collaborations and potential investments worth about RM10.3 billion, surpassing the RM8 billion target. — Bernama

Not only does the Mate XT 2 adopt the inward-folding form factor used on Samsung's Galaxy Z TriFold, it's also the first foldable to include a privacy-enhancing display, much like the one Samsung added to the Galaxy S26 Ultra this year.

49eb6546f3d26d7c: GERIK: The six hikers reported missing while taking part in the Trans Gerah Expedition at Mount Gerah, Kelantan, have been found safe, police confirmed today.
District police chief Superintendent Abdul Samad Othman confirmed the matter after rescuers managed to establish contact with a mountain guide accompanying the group.
"We have managed to contact the mountain guide, and everyone is safe.
"All the hikers are safe, and we will carry out the rescue process," he said when contacted by Buletin TV3.
He said a ground rescue team will be deployed to the group's location to assist them.
A rescue team will be deployed by helicopter to a nearby camp, where they will trek to reach the victims.
"The rescue team will head up today as well," he said.
Earlier, search and rescue operations for the six were intensified, with a Fire and Rescue Department Mi-17 aircraft from the Subang Air Base scheduled to conduct an aerial survey along the trail.
The missing group comprised a family of four, including two children aged 9 and 13, and two mountain guides.
c247ba81050dea48: SEREMBAN: The Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) has busted a drug-processing syndicate suspected of producing RM27.5 million worth of methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) in Seremban and Kuala Lumpur.

Bukit Aman NCID director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the syndicate's 52-year-old main suspect was shot dead after he allegedly fired at the raiding team at a terraced house here about 1.30pm yesterday.
He said the rented house had been used as a laboratory to process drugs since early this year.
Police seized suspected MDMA comprising 64.49kg of liquid, 5.2kg of drug lumps, 7.9kg of drug pills and 104.8kg of drug powder, as well as various drug-processing equipment.
"We believe the suspect obtained the drugs with the assistance of other syndicate members by bringing in drug-processing precursors from abroad.
"The suspect who was shot dead also had the expertise to process these chemicals into MDMA or ecstasy," he said at a press conference at the Seremban district police headquarters here today.
Hussein said the suspect was believed to have extensive experience in drug-related activities, with his involvement detected since the 1990s.
He also had three previous arrest and imprisonment records under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
Hussein said the suspect was also wanted under Section 3(1) of the Kidnapping Act 1961 and had a previous criminal record under Section 448 of the Penal Code.
He said the syndicate's modus operandi was to use residential areas with low population density to process and distribute drugs while concealing its activities from the authorities.
The drugs were believed to have been intended for local and overseas markets, while police were tracking several other suspects believed to have fled abroad.
Meanwhile, Hussein said police conducted two separate raids in Seremban 2 and Kuchai Lama, Kuala Lumpur, resulting in the arrest of a 32-year-old woman and a 35-year-old man.

Both tested positive for drugs, with the woman testing positive for methamphetamine and the man for tetrahydrocannabinol (THC). Both also had previous criminal records, including drug-related offences.
They were remanded for seven days until Sept 13.
Hussein said police also seized three cars and the case was being investigated under Section 307 of the Penal Code and Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
He said the seizure could indirectly curb the distribution of drugs to more than 400,000 users.
d8ed90c91bc3d5cd: BERLIN: The Alternative for Germany appealed on Monday to lawmakers from Chancellor Friedrich Merz's conservatives to support its bid to rule Saxony-Anhalt after the far-right party surged into first place in the eastern German state's election.

The anti-immigrant, pro-Russia AfD won nearly 44 per cent of the vote, official results showed, an outcome that underlined the deep unpopularity of Merz's ruling coalition and also triggered alarm among Germany's neighbours, France and Poland.

However, the party — which wants to deport immigrants, halt support for Ukraine and ditch the euro — has fallen short of an absolute majority in the state legislature, winning 39 of the 83 seats, and hopes to win over individual conservative lawmakers.

The election result raises serious questions about the longstanding refusal of Germany's mainstream parties, including Merz's Christian Democrats (CDU), to work with the AfD, a policy known as the "firewall."
The AfD says this is undemocratic.

"Politics always means compromise," national AfD co-leader Tino Chrupalla told German broadcaster ARD, appealing to CDU lawmakers to make a "centre-right conservative majority" in Saxony-Anhalt possible.
The CDU needs to ask itself what conclusions it draws from this disastrous election result, he added.
"Partisan games really ought to be a thing of the past," he told German radio, referring to the firewall policy.

Ulrich Siegmund, the party's lead candidate in the state, said he hoped to become Saxony-Anhalt's state premier if the AfD could build a stable majority in the legislature, and said it would hold discussions with various parliamentary groups there.
The only German party that has signalled readiness to work with the AfD is the populist left-wing BSW, which on Monday echoed Chrupalla's criticism of the "firewall" policy.

"Even the mere attempt to forge another 'firewall' coalition (by the other mainstream parties to keep the AfD out of power in Saxony-Anhalt) would be an affront to the voters," said Sahra Wagenknecht, the face of the left-wing populist BSW.

The BSW shares the AfD's hostility towards mass immigration, which it says undermines local workers' rights, and also advocates for ending Germany's support for Ukraine and restoring ties with Moscow.
The BSW could help clear the way for Siegmund to become state premier by abstaining in a parliamentary vote.
That could allow him to head a minority government, although Siegmund has previously rejected such a scenario.
Germany's intelligence services have branded the AfD as "extremist", allowing them to step up surveillance of the country's biggest opposition party.
The AfD strongly rejects the label.

Saxony-Anhalt is a relatively small state, and one of the poorest in Germany's former communist east, but Alice Weidel, the AfD's other national co-leader, hailed Sunday's result as a milestone and said her party aimed to win at least 40 per cent in the next national election, due in 2029.
In the first international reaction to the election result, French Finance Minister Roland Lescure told RTL radio it "sends out a very, very worrying signal."

"This shows that we face a major challenge in the face of a populist wave which is spreading around the world today and which we must resist," said Lescure, whose own country holds national elections next year that could see far-right veteran Marine Le Pen become president of France.
Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski also described Sunday's outcome in Saxony-Anhalt as "a very worrying sign."
The AfD won 43.8 per cent of the vote, according to the official election results, more than doubling its support from the last state election in 2021.
The CDU's share almost halved to 17.2 per cent, with about 83,000 former CDU voters switching to the AfD.

CDU state candidate Sven Schulze attributed part of his party's poor performance to developments in Berlin, where Merz — the most unpopular chancellor in German history — is struggling to revive Germany's sluggish economic growth.

The euro was little changed in Monday trade but analysts are closely monitoring the surge in support for far-right parties across Europe, noting that the AfD wants to take Germany out of the common currency.
"This development is dangerous for the longer term stability of the single currency," XTB research director Kathleen Brooks said.

"The next few years could see waves of political change in Europe and a shift to the right in the two largest economies. This may not be a problem for FX traders today, but it is a problem for tomorrow."

3ff5db0152dcdbc4: SHAH ALAM: Twelve men have been charged following two separate gang-related brawls in Shah Alam that left one dead and another severely injured, Selangor police said today.

State police chief Shazeli Kahar said the suspects, aged between 23 and 46, were arrested in an operation conducted across Selangor and Johor between Aug 14 and Aug 28. Police are still hunting for 10 more suspects, he added.
Of the 12, eight were charged with murder, while four others were charged with rioting with weapons following a slashing incident in Sri Muda, he said.
"Some suspects were released due to insufficient evidence," Shazeli told a press conference here.
Shazeli said that while the two incidents were unrelated, both were linked to gangsterism. The fatal clash stemmed from a turf war while the slashing incident resulted from a misunderstanding.
In the Aug 25 Taman Alam Megah case, a 23-year-old man was slashed before being hit by a Perodua Alza, resulting in his death. Eight men, including two brothers, were charged with murder on Sept 4.
In the Aug 13 Sri Muda case, a 38-year-old man was badly injured after being slashed near a petrol station by several men. An imitation pistol was also used in the incident.
Police are searching for seven suspects linked to the murder and three tied to the Sri Muda assault.
3a87369131ccc4bf: KUALA LUMPUR: Police has proposed amendments to outdated laws and tougher penalties, including rotan, for online scammers.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said stronger deterrent measures were crucial to curbing the growing threat of cybercrime and protecting public safety.
He said the penalties currently imposed by the courts were too lenient and failed to deter masterminds and members of scam syndicates.
"Arrests are being made continuously nationwide, but the penalties imposed are so minimal that they do not instil fear in criminals.
"This matter has been raised with the ministry and the government so that legislative changes can be made in line with technological developments and international standards," he said.
He said this in his closing speech at the PDRM and Media Prima Berhad Strategic Communications Collaboration Programme at Bukit Aman today.
6226b3414315eb5a: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia traded higher today, supported by renewed buying interest in selected banking and telecommunications heavyweights, an analyst said.

142dd6f24660ada9: LETTERS: It is no secret that Malaysia's healthcare sector has faced increasingly serious talent-retention challenges, especially in recent years, both in the private and public sectors.
On Aug 15, the Health Minister said that 10,557 of the 73,281 nurse positions in health facilities were vacant.

At the same time, the Health Ministry's nursing workforce fell by about 1,200 between 2022 and 2024, from 71,434 to 70,234. Malaysian nurses are also being recruited for overseas positions, particularly in Singapore and the Gulf, while countries such as the United Kingdom and Australia provide attractive pathways for internationally trained nurses, offering substantially higher remuneration and, in some cases, stronger benefits, work-life balance, and career opportunities.

In my four decades of practice, having worked alongside hundreds of nurses and doctors, I can say with great confidence that a majority of Malaysian healthcare professionals are not in this profession simply for the money. Many, if not most, are driven by a deep sense of duty, a desire to serve their country, and a genuine passion for caring for others.

With this in mind, I believe that retaining our nurses is crucial, and one of the most important things we can do to retain them is to ensure the well-being of nurses so that they feel safe, supported, and valued at their places of work in private or public hospitals.
Building a formal nurses-safety framework

Malaysia has spent considerable effort building a formal patient-safety framework, the Malaysian Patient Safety Goals (MPSG), to address key patient-safety priorities. But healthcare staff safety, especially that of nurses, has not, from my observation, enjoyed the same degree of institutionalisation or visibility as patient safety.
Nurses face daily exposure to infectious diseases and, in a lot of cases, physical and verbal abuse, harassment, and bullying from colleagues, patients, and patients' families.
While hospitals have a responsibility to provide a safe working environment, patients, their families and the wider public also have a role to play in treating nurses with respect.

Nurses are trained healthcare professionals. They should not be expected to perform every non-clinical task simply because they are available, nor should they be subjected to shouting, verbal abuse, or intimidation.

Such incidents are far too common in Malaysia. When nurses are repeatedly exposed to stress, hostility, and abuse, it can take a toll on their mental and emotional well-being, and ultimately, affect the quality of the care they provide. This is true for any profession, in fact. Everyone deserves to be treated with dignity in performing their duties.
The cost of retention and turnover

A longstanding issue that needs greater attention in nurse retention is whether Malaysians fully recognise the true cost of healthcare. Yes, medicines, equipment, hospital buildings and medical technology contribute to healthcare costs, and the increase of it, but we must also factor in the people who deliver care.

Nurses make up the largest group of healthcare professionals in Malaysia, with 141,255 nurses recorded across the public and private sectors in 2024, an increase of 2.3 per cent from the previous year.

In the race to "reduce healthcare costs", we cannot do so by undervaluing the people who deliver care. If we do not adequately remunerate and retain nurses, our healthcare system will inevitably struggle to maintain the quality and standard of care that Malaysians deserve.
Nurse turnover can be costly. While Malaysia-specific figures are not currently available, US data can provide a helpful benchmark.

A 2026 US report covering 527 hospitals estimated that replacing one bedside registered nurse costs about USD 60,090, with the average hospital spending between USD 4.2 million and USD 6.2 million a year on nurse turnover.
The report also found that every 1 per cent increase or decrease in nurse turnover could cost or save a hospital about USD 295,000 annually.
Another US study found that hospitals spent about USD16,736 per nurse each year on turnover linked to burnout, compared with USD 11,592 at hospitals that introduced programmes to reduce burnout.
Nurses in hospitals with such programmes also stayed for about 3.5 years, compared with 2.9 years without them, suggesting that reducing burnout could lower turnover-related costs by about 30%.
The takeaway from this is not that Malaysia will incur the same costs as the United States. It is that staff turnover has a substantial economic cost.
Nurses wellbeing and safety programmes
A well-designed staff-wellbeing programme could potentially be a worthwhile investment when compared with the costs associated with having to repeatedly recruit and onboard.
This raises the question of what can be done to safeguard nurses' workplace safety and mental and emotional well-being while making employment in Malaysian hospitals a sustainable career.
The Health Ministry's own Nursing Strategic Plan 2026–2036, launched on June 9, recognises much of this.

It sets out 17 strategies and 44 initiatives, and names burnout and the migration of skilled staff among the challenges it is designed to confront. The Health Minister was right to say the ministry can no longer rely on cosmetic approaches or temporary fixes.

The next step now is implementation. Since the plan identifies burnout as a core challenge, what is needed is effective commitments on workplace-violence reporting, mental-health support and roster design.

Confidential mental-health support that nurses will actually use needs to be in place. That said, support also must be accessible and designed around the reality of what nurses are facing in their workplace, rather than as an administrative programme for staff.

In addition, the Healthy Ministry may consider whether existing systems can be strengthened to provide staff-safety reporting with greater national visibility and standardisation, while ensuring that reporting is confidential and non-punitive for victims.

Some private hospitals are already giving nurses more say in how they are rostered. This is an approach that deserves wider consideration because having greater control and predictability over work schedules can help reduce fatigue and stress and give nurses a more sustainable work-life balance.
The World Health Organisation's Global Patient Safety Action Plan 2021–2030 recognises that patient safety depends in part on creating safe working environments for health workers.
Occupational safety and healthcare organisations internationally have similarly emphasised the importance of protecting healthcare workers from violence, burnout and other workplace risks.
At some point, every one of us will be a patient, and we will depend on nurses to provide safe, professional and compassionate care when we are most vulnerable.
Protecting nurses and their wellbeing is therefore also about protecting the quality and safety of care we can all expect to receive.

As such, I urge all Malaysian hospitals to take the wellbeing and safety of nurses seriously, and for all Malaysians to treat nurses with dignity. We have a responsibility to protect and support our nurses, especially those who choose to stay and serve despite the "greener grass" abroad.
Datuk Dr Kuljit Singh
President of the Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia (APHM)

a7e124744a1ba784: KUALA LUMPUR: The China Masters witnessed a historic all-Hong Kong final, with Jason Gunawan outplaying Lee Cheuk Yiu for the title.
But significantly, the occasion was also the result of the hard work of two Malaysians — Wong Choong Hann and Loh Wei Sheng — on the sidelines on Sunday.

Hong Kong head coach Choong Hann was in tears by courtside as world No. 32 Jason wrapped up his straight-game 21-9, 21-16 win at the Shenzhen Arena to become Hong Kong's first men's shuttler to win a Super 750 title.
The Malaysian resigned as the BA of Malaysia (BAM) singles coaching director in 2023 before assuming his role as Hong Kong's chief coach in the same year.
Choong Hann, who said the tears were simply the joy of witnessing such a success, also gave due credit to Wei Sheng, who runs the men's singles programme.

"It (the tears) was simply pure joy of witnessing two of our men's singles players in an all-Hong Kong final. A memorable moment as it is Hong Kong's first men's singles Super 750 title," said Choong Hann.
"Wei Sheng is our men's singles coach and 90 per cent of the practice routine and decisions are coached and planned by him, actually.
"I'm just the remaining 10 per cent for the past one year or so, more in a mentoring role. In fact, the credit goes to him, actually!
"Sometimes, we do rotate our touring (for tournaments) routine among coaches due to some internal planning, and we complement each other.
"I would also like to credit the assistant coach Agus (Hariyanto), who has been working together with Wei Sheng, for this success."
The success is also timely and, although Choong Hann did not predict any medals, he said the China Masters crown is a confidence booster ahead of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Sept 19-Oct 4.
"This result does boost confidence heading towards the Asian Games. Our players' good spirits and motivated. We believe our players will give their best for the team," added Choong Hann.
The higher-ranked Cheuk Yiu (No. 25) and Angus Ng Ka Long (No. 32) will be playing in the individual events in Aichi-Nagoya while Jason will join them in the men's team event.
Wei Nan remains the only men's singles medallist for Hong Kong at the Asiad after he secured bronze in the 2014 Games in Incheon, South Korea.

7e9206795c4d3975: GENEVA, Sept 7 — The United Nations rights chief on Monday demanded accountability for swelling numbers of deaths in US immigration custody, and urged Washington to halt deportations to places where people face “irreparable harm”.
Speaking before the UN Human Rights Council, Volker Turk highlighted that “four more people have died in US immigration custody since my last update to this council” in June.
That meant there had been “a total of 23 deaths in 2026 alone”, he said, insisting that “there needs to be accountability for these deaths”.
US President Donald Trump has made combating illegal immigration a top priority of his second term, with authorities rounding up thousands of people and expanding detention centres.
A joint report by Human Rights Watch and Physicians for Human Rights in June said that the rate of people dying in ICE custody has reached its highest level in over a decade amid Trump’s crackdown.
The UN rights chief on Monday also called out a range of other US immigration enforcement practices, including forcing migrant returns to dangerous places and to countries they had no connection to.

“I urge the United States to halt the return of people to places where they could suffer irreparable harm, including Haiti, and to ensure due process for all removals to third countries,” he told the council.

The UN rights chief also voiced alarm at the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agency’s reported plans to “equip immigration agents with electric shock gloves”, warning this would “increase the violence associated with their operations”.

The plan to purchase the shock gloves, which was first reported by The Associated Press, calls for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), the ICE parent agency, to spend $10 to $20 million on what are described as “distraction and de-escalation” devices.
ICE has come in for criticism for a series of fatal shootings during enforcement operations, including those of two American citizens in Minnesota in January who were involved in anti-ICE protests.
Critics have focused on the forceful tactics used by ICE agents in rounding up migrants and on an alleged lowering of the standards of training for new recruits. — AFP

af9118d4240c33bf: JAKARTA: The Sunda Strait remains safe from a tsunami threat amid ongoing activity at Mount Anak Krakatau, with no tsunami detected as authorities continue round-the-clock monitoring.
The volcano is located in the strait, between the Indonesian islands of Java and Sumatra.

Indonesia's Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) said its high-frequency (HF) radar monitoring placed the probability of a tsunami in the Sunda Strait in the low category as of 8 am Monday.
"The Sunda Strait crossing route remains in safe condition," the agency said in a statement on Monday.
BMKG Acting Deputy for Geophysics Ardhasena Sopaheluwakan said monitoring at 20 tsunami gauges around the strait also showed no unusual changes in sea level that would indicate a tsunami.

While the gauges showed no indication of a tsunami, he said BMKG's other instruments recorded increased volcanic lightning and geomagnetic disturbances between midnight and 4 am, although both were less intense than during the first eruption on Sept 4.

On sea conditions, BMKG Acting Deputy for Meteorology Andri Ramdhani said surface currents were predominantly moving southwest towards the Indian Ocean at between 0.4 and 0.9 knots, with waves measuring between 0.3 and 1.2 metres.

Looking ahead, he said wave heights in the Sunda Strait were forecast to range between 0.5 and 2 metres from Sept 8 to 13, with generally clear to partly cloudy conditions expected around Anak Krakatau and the strait.

Andri said BMKG had issued 39 Significant Meteorological Information (SIGMET) advisories for aviation since the first eruption on Sept 4, with the latest showing ash reaching 4,572 metres and moving westward towards Sumatra and the Indian Ocean at 15 knots.
"Based on an analysis of Himawari-9 satellite imagery at 9 am, the wind pattern generally pushed Mount Anak Krakatau's volcanic ash westward," he said.
ffebac2808c8cb20: KUALA LUMPUR: A woman’s suit against developer Oasis Garden Development Sdn Bhd over alleged defects in her M-City Ampang unit will proceed to trial after the High Court set aside an order striking out her claim.
Judicial Commissioner DR Shoba Rajah said Ramaswree Duraisamy, who purchased a unit in 2012, had raised genuine issues that could not be summarily determined without hearing evidence.
Ramaswree had appealed against the sessions court’s decision on June 3, 2025, which allowed Oasis Garden’s application to strike out her entire claim.

She sued the developer over alleged water leakage and other defects in her residential unit, seeking a declaration that the sale and purchase agreement had been breached, and an order compelling rectification works and damages.

Her claims included RM213,000 in lost rental income, RM27,193 in maintenance charges and general damages for hardship and inconvenience. The unit was handed over to Ramaswree in May 2016 but remained unoccupied for a considerable period.

She claimed she discovered serious defects, including water leakage which damaged the walls, tiles, furniture and ceilings, around 2019. Although remedial works were later carried out, she said the defects recurred in early 2024.
A subsequent investigation report commissioned by the developer recorded water seepage from joints between the concrete slab and beam above a wall of the unit.
Oasis Garden argued that the claim was time-barred because the six-year limitation period should have begun when vacant possession was delivered in 2016.
But in her 20-page judgment, Shoba said the question of when the cause of action accrued, particularly where latent defects were concerned, raised a serious legal issue.
She also said there was a factual dispute over when the defects were first discovered, which could only fairly be determined through evidence at trial.
On the developer’s investigation report, Shoba said it was too early to determine whether the findings amounted to an admission of defective workmanship or negligence.
She said expert evidence and cross-examination might be required to establish whether the seepage resulted from defective construction, poor maintenance or other causes.
The judge also found that Ramaswree’s claim for lost rental income should not be struck out merely because she had yet to produce evidence proving the loss.
"Whether she genuinely intended to rent out the unit and whether the defects frustrated those efforts are matters for trial.”
Shoba concluded that the disputed factual and evidential issues required a full hearing, where witnesses could give evidence and be cross-examined.
Ambbi Sundrambal Balakrishnan represented Ramaswree while Amanda Rachel Chong appeared for Oasis Garden.
549575bd9145cf20: THE HAGUE, Sept 7 — Germany on Monday urged the United Nations’ top court to throw out a case against it by Nicaragua, which has accused Berlin of “facilitating genocide” in Gaza with its support of Israel.
Julia Monar, representing Germany at the International Court of Justice, said judges lacked the jurisdiction to rule on the case and dismissed Nicaragua’s accusations as “inaccurate and distorted.”
Nicaragua has dragged Germany before the ICJ in The Hague, arguing that its backing of Israel, notably in terms of arms exports, contravenes the 1948 UN Genocide Convention.
Opening four days of hearings, Monar told ICJ judges that “the conditions on which this court’s jurisdiction is based are not met in this case.”

“For the first time in the history of this court, it is being asked to adjudicate a case that is twice removed from a classic bilateral dispute,” Monar told the court, which rules on legal arguments between countries.
“Neither Nicaragua nor Germany is a party to the conflict that forms the real subject matter of this case, the Israeli-Palestinian conflict,” noted Monar.
This meant that the court should declare itself incompetent to rule on the case, argued Monar.

The case dates back to 2024, following the start of Israel’s offensive in Gaza. Nicaragua urged ICJ judges to impose emergency measures to force Berlin to halt all aid to Israel, in particular military equipment.
The court threw out Nicaragua’s request in April of that year, saying “the circumstances, as they now present themselves” did not justify emergency orders.

The case is nevertheless ongoing and Germany is now seeking to have it removed, either by persuading judges they do not have the power to rule in the case or that Nicaragua’s argument does not stack up.
Berlin has filed so-called “preliminary objections to the jurisdiction of the Court and to the admissibility of certain claims” presented by Nicaragua, according to an ICJ statement.
‘Inaccurate and distorted’
Addressing that “admissibility”, Monar said: “Nicaragua’s factual statements are not only inapposite at this stage of the proceedings, but also create an inaccurate and distorted picture.”
“All German exports of military technology and equipment to Israel — as to any country — are subject to strict licensing requirements which exceed international requirements,” she said.
Monar noted Germany’s “unwavering support for the existence and security of the State of Israel” but also said it was one of the world’s largest bilateral donors to the Palestinian Territories.
Germany seeks a “lasting peace” in Gaza, a goal Monar said was shared by Nicaragua.
“However, Germany has serious doubts that the case brought to your court by Nicaragua would in any way bring us any closer to this shared goal,” she said.
“By way of consequence, Germany respectfully requests the court reject Nicaragua’s claims,” concluded Monar.
During hearings at the court in April 2024, Nicaragua said Germany was “pathetic” to provide aid to Gaza while also simultaneously furnishing Israel with weapons.
Nicaragua’s ambassador to the Netherlands, Carlos Jose Arguello Gomez, told the court at that time: “Germany seems not to be able to differentiate between self-defence and genocide.”
The court will hold four days of hearings at the Peace Palace where the court sits, with Nicaragua responding on Tuesday.
It takes on average six months for the court to hand down a ruling in such cases.
The court could either side with Germany and throw out the case completely or rule against Berlin, meaning the case would then be considered “on the merits” in more detail.
This procedure is separate from a high-profile case also before the ICJ, in which South Africa has accused Israel of perpetrating genocide in Gaza, which Israel denies.
The ICJ’s rulings are binding but it has no power to enforce them.
For example, it has ordered Russia to stop its invasion of Ukraine, a demand that has fallen on deaf ears in the Kremlin. — AFP
0597ba6dead33c3f: KOTA BARU: A Form Two student died after being electrocuted while retrieving a fishing hook stuck on an electrical wire in Kampung Langgar yesterday.
Mohamad Amiruddin Anwar Md Azam, 14, a student of SMK Sultan Ismail, was pronounced dead at the emergency unit of Hospital Raja Perempuan Zainab II (HRPZII) while receiving treatment.
His 10-year-old cousin, Ahmad Eizz Rayyan Ahmad Ridhuwan, who was also electrocuted while trying to help him, is being treated at the hospital's burn unit and is in stable condition.
Amiruddin's mother, Norhabibi Jaafar, 52, said the incident occurred around 4pm near a water channel about 200 metres from their home.
"My son went home to fetch an aluminium pole, which is normally used to pick fruit, before returning to retrieve the hook stuck on the electrical wire. He was electrocuted," she said.
"After being electrocuted, my son remained standing rigid, holding the aluminium pole.
"His cousin tried to help him but was also electrocuted, and both fell into the water channel," she said.
Amiruddin's younger brother, Azamuddin Azwa, 10, who witnessed the incident, ran home to alert their mother.
"I rushed to the scene and found several people performing CPR on my son before the ambulance arrived.
"His body was buried at Tanah Perkuburan Islam Mukim Langgar at 9.20am today," Norhabibi said.
Meanwhile, Noor Elhaam Ramli, 35, the mother of Ahmad Eizz Rayyan, said her son was in good health and able to eat, although doctors were monitoring his cardiac condition.
He has also undergone 2 electrocardiogram (ECG) tests.
"He is asking to go home to see his cousin one last time since they were very close," said Noor Elhaam.
Witness Wan Roslinda Che Deris, 47, said she was travelling from Kota Baru to her in-laws' home when a man flagged her down for help.
"My husband and another man helped lift both victims.
"When my husband lifted one, the body was already rigid, but his legs still felt warm. We performed CPR while waiting for the ambulance," she said.
4f3da6f1d06adfa7: NIBONG TEBAL: SJKC Boon Beng has received RM500,000 under the prime minister's special allocation to support construction of an additional block at the school.

Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the allocation, announced following a visit to the school with the prime minister's political secretary Chan Ming Kai, would help the school and community continue the expansion project.
"While RM500,000 will not cover the entire cost, it will help the school and community continue efforts that have already begun," she said in her social media posting.
The additional block will comprise 12 classrooms and other facilities, with the overall project costing RM8.6 million.
Fadhlina said the government's approach to education was based on addressing the actual needs faced by schools, including repairs, space shortages and inadequate facilities.
"Whatever is written on the school gate, those studying inside are still Malaysian children," she said.
She thanked Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim for his continued attention to education.
Last year, the school marked its 100th anniversary, celebrating a century of contributions to national education and the local community.

Fadhlina had then said that the school, in her parliamentary constituency in Nibong Tebal, was a school of choice for parents from various ethnic backgrounds, reflecting its longstanding role in Malaysia's education landscape.
ab423e8116b13b90: GENEVA: The United Nations rights chief warned Monday that artificial intelligence could pose an "existential threat to humanity", demanding immediate action to reduce the risks.
Speaking before the UN Human Rights Council, Volker Turk warned that humans currently faced "unfamiliar, even unprecedented" threats to their rights.
"The need for AI governance is widely acknowledged, but where is the action?" he asked, warning that "delay only benefits the massive tech companies, their owners and enablers".
Turk decried that "a handful of men has almost unlimited power over AI, which we are repeatedly told has unimaginable computing capacity".
"They talk about freedom, but on closer inspection, this turns out to be little more than the freedom to exploit our data," the rights chief said.
Turk warned in particular that "AI that escapes its testing environment or blackmails developers to prevent itself from being turned off, is AI that is too powerful".

He appeared to be alluding to revelations in July that OpenAI agents had escaped supposedly controlled environments and had broken into servers of Hugging Face, a widely used platform where programmers share AI software.
That episode shook the tech world and revived calls for tighter regulation and oversight of AI.
Anthropic, Meta and other companies have reported similar incidents while testing agents.
"I share the concerns of industry insiders that advanced AI could pose an existential risk to humanity," Turk said.
"I am calling here, today, for an all-out effort to put cast iron guarantees in place around the safety and security of AI, before it is too late."
The UN rights chief said he would be writing to AI companies in coming days "to urge them to take the steps that are within their control to reduce risks now".
At a minimum, he said, "we need countries hosting AI and those involved in its supply chains to come together around agreed red lines".
"We need independent verification, and much stronger collaboration on security within the industry," he said.
"We also need to consider the human rights impacts of AI on employment practices, on fundamental principles of democracy, and on our environment."
83c465ba656f35cf: KUALA LUMPUR: Several supporter groups or ultras have submitted memorandums to clubs and state football associations (FAs) on Monday.
The action was taken by the supporter groups involved to state their stance and urge the club or FA management not to choose to remain silent on the integrity of Malaysian football.

Among the supporter groups involved are Ultra Selangor, who submitted a memorandum to Selangor FC, Ultras Nogori submitted it to Negri Sembilan FC, Ultras Tranung to Terengganu FC, Gate H Boys to Kelantan Red Warrior and Ultras Panthers to Penang FC.

The North Borneo Ultras (NBU) group submitted their memorandum to the Sabah Football Association (SAFA), while The Supporters and Ultras Kedah 2009 (UK09) submitted their memorandums to the Perak Football Association and the Kedah Football Association, respectively.

Through the memorandum shared by the supporter groups involved on social media sites, among the matters stated or questioned in the memorandum were especially related to the forgery case involving seven Harimau Malaya players previously.
The supporter group also disputed the decision of the Malaysian Football League (MFL) to change the player quota on the opening day of the 2026-2027 Super League.
"On Aug 21, the MFL Board of Directors approved an additional five local player slots, increasing the maximum squad from 33 to 38 players," according to a memorandum from the Ultras Tranung group.
"The MFL stated that the decision was made following applications from Johor Darul Ta'zim and Kuching City, before the same facility was given to all clubs.
"The MFL also confirmed that the minimum registration for each club remains 20 players and the first window closes on Sept 3."
The supporter group questioned the issue regarding KL City registering only 12 players following the registration restrictions imposed by the FIFA on the club.
In addition, they also asked for a clear line so that forgery is not normalised, loopholes are not exploited, integrity is not compromised and clubs are not silent.
e82f8f3c4a6afa99: BELGRADE: Thousands of people gathered in front of a church in Belgrade to pay respects to former Bosnian Serb general Ratko Mladic, who died last week while serving a life sentence for genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity.

Mladic remains a revered figure among many Serbs in Serbia and in Bosnia's autonomous Serb Republic, despite his convictions linked to his role in the 1995 Srebrenica massacre and in the siege of Sarajevo.
People carrying Serbian flags and pictures of Mladic wearing a traditional Serbian military cap arrived in front of the church to light candles early on Monday, hours before his scheduled burial.
Free bus services were offered from Bosnia and most towns in Serbia for anyone who wanted to pay their respects.

Mladic's coffin was displayed inside the church and six men, mainly war veterans from Serbia and Bosnia, took turns guarding it. Mladic's wife, son, and grandchildren stood inside receiving condolences.
"Time will tell, time is the best judge who will show what kind of person is who and to whom," said Belgrade resident Jovan Vincic, who had come to the church.
Conflicts triggered by break-up of Yugoslavia
Mladic's death has stirred up strong feelings linking back to the breakup of Yugoslavia and the ethnic conflicts that ensued in the Balkans.

Mladic was found guilty by the UN International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia of genocide for his role in the 1995 Srebrenica massacre, in which about 8,000 Bosniak Muslim men and boys were killed after Bosnian Serb forces overran the UN-designated enclave.
He was also convicted over the 43-month siege of Sarajevo, during which about 10,000 people were killed.

Last week, EU enlargement commissioner Marta Kos postponed her visit to Serbia because of what she said was the "glorification" of Mladic after his death, including the use of a government plane to return him to Serbia.
Serbian president Aleksandar Vucic dismissed those statements, but did not say whether he would attend Monday's funeral.
The service was scheduled to be conducted by the Patriarch of the Serbian Orthodox church at noon, after which Mladic will be buried in a nearby cemetery beside his daughter, who died in 1994.
In Sarajevo, meanwhile, the funeral rekindled painful memories of the war.

"It is really horrible that this is taking place there (in Belgrade) because I know there are normal people who are against it," said Zdravka Gvozdjar, a retired pharmacist whose 9-year-old son was killed during the Sarajevo siege by a grenade fired by the Mladic-led forces, one among more than 1,000 children killed in the city.
"Mladic ... only deserved to be erased from memory for good, not to be ... promoted as a hero," she said. "He should be remembered only as a butcher," she added.

0e62b664073e2543: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 7 — Air quality in parts of Penang island reached an unhealthy level today, with its Air Pollutant Index (API) reading climbing to 142 at 3pm.
Penang housing and environment committee chairman Datuk Seri Sundarajoo Somu said the Minden air-quality monitoring station on the island began recording unhealthy readings at 9am.
“The reading continued to rise, reaching 142 at 3pm,” he said in a statement today.
He said the station recorded readings of between 82 and 142 throughout the day.
Meanwhile, monitoring stations in Seberang Perai, Seberang Jaya and Balik Pulau recorded moderate readings of between 55 and 91.
Minden was the only one of Penang’s four monitoring stations to record unhealthy air quality.
Sundarajoo said Penang’s air quality had generally remained at good to moderate levels between September 4 and 6.
He said preliminary information from the ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre showed that 737 hotspots were recorded in Sumatra and another 540 in Kalimantan during the period.
Hotspots were also detected in several Malaysian states.
“The increase in hotspots in Sumatra and Kalimantan indicates more significant fire activity in the region,” he said.
However, Sundarajoo said hotspot numbers alone could not determine Penang’s air quality.
He said the impact on the state depended on factors such as wind direction and speed, atmospheric conditions and rainfall distribution.
“Intermittent rain had helped keep Penang’s air quality within good to moderate levels during the monitoring period,” he said.
PM₁₀ was identified as the dominant pollutant, although its concentration remained at a moderate level.
He advised the public to monitor official API readings for their respective areas through the Department of Environment’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS).
He also urged the public not to rely on unverified information or social media posts.
He advised the public to avoid open burning, including burning rubbish, dried leaves and agricultural waste, and to report such activities immediately.
Children, senior citizens and those with respiratory conditions should reduce strenuous outdoor activities if API readings rise.
The public should also reduce the time spent outdoors, keep doors and windows closed, and wear suitable face masks if air quality worsens.
Sundarajoo said the public should avoid activities that could worsen air pollution and reduce unnecessary vehicle use.
He encouraged residents to use public transport, carpool or choose more sustainable ways of travelling.
He said the Department of Environment and other relevant agencies will continue monitoring air quality and regional hotspots.
53a2272833c1158a: KUALA LUMPUR: The Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) MAS-01 is en route from Kathmandu to Trishuli Bazar, Nepal, to carry out a Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) mission.

National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim said the team was being escorted by the Nepalese Army and the journey to Trishuli Bazar would take about three hours.
He said that their team consists of 11 officers and personnel, travelling in a 10-tonne truck and two vehicles.
"The journey will take three hours, depending on road and traffic conditions," he said when contacted today.
On Saturday, the 11 Smart officers and personnel departed for Nepal aboard a Royal Malaysian Air Force A400M aircraft from the Subang Air Base at approximately 9 am.
The team brought along search and rescue equipment to support ground operations in the affected zones.
To date, over 5,000 individuals are still reported missing, while 1,300 have been confirmed dead in the disaster.
Of those still missing, 55 are Malaysian citizens.
